subject.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine

question: Should OpenClaw core keep this PR as the in-core rescue-watchdog candidate after a current-main rebase and real-host proof, or redirect the remaining watchdog direction to the broader recovery issue or external/operator-managed recovery?
rationale: The PR is not just a small bug fix: it adds a new core cron payload and automatic repair/restart capability across service-control and command-execution boundaries, so maintainers need to confirm the product/security direction after the concrete rebase blockers are fixed.

options.title: Continue Core Review After Rebase
options.body: Keep this PR open as the candidate, but require the current protocol/store/command-cron fixes, security review, and real-host recovery proof before merge.

options.title: Redirect To Canonical Recovery Discussion
options.body: Close or pause this branch and track the desired self-healing shape in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36314 before accepting a new implementation.

options.title: Keep Recovery External For Now
options.body: Ask contributors to keep watchdog recovery as operator-managed tooling/docs until core has a smaller approved API or product boundary.

recommendation.title: Continue Core Review After Rebase
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open as the candidate, but require the current protocol/store/command-cron fixes, security review, and real-host recovery proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history signal on daemon/recovery lifecycle surfaces and is a good owner for the product/security boundary decision.
